title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: M is a motive over an algebraically closed field k that admits embeddings into C (the 'alg. clos' is an interlinear insertion). By 'place v of k' Grothendieck evidently means a complex embedding v: k -> C. Each embedding v gives a Betti realization with an integral structure, M_v^Z = H_B(v^*M, Z). Via the Artin comparison theorem between Betti and étale cohomology, M_v^Z ⊗ Ẑ is identified with ∏_ℓ M(ℓ), the integral ℓ-adic realizations, which do not depend on v. So each M_v^Z sits as a lattice, and M_v^Q as a Q-structure, inside the one adelic module ∏_ℓ M(ℓ).

Problem posed: describe the relations among the lattices M_{v_1}^Z, ..., M_{v_n}^Z for several embeddings v_1, ..., v_n. This is the cohomological side of Serre's phenomenon that conjugate varieties can have different topology.

Method (Tannakian):
1. Fix a reference fibre functor ξ over Q on the Tannakian category generated by M, written M -> M_{ξ_0}. It comes with functorial isomorphisms ξ ⊗ Q_ℓ ≅ (ℓ-adic realization).
2. Each Betti functor ξ_{v_i} is also a Q-valued fibre functor. Hence P_i = Isom^⊗(ξ, ξ_{v_i}) is a principal homogeneous space (torsor) over Q under the motivic Galois group G = G^f_{M,ξ_0} = Aut^⊗(ξ).
3. The étale comparison isomorphisms give a canonical Q̂-point of ∏ P_i, where Q̂ = ∏_ℓ Q_ℓ.
4. Let G act diagonally (marginal insertion). Since the reference functor was arbitrary, the invariant object is the image point in [(∏ P_i)/G](Q̂).
5. After several struck-out attempts he forgets the G-structure and takes the image in the double coset space GL(m,Ẑ)^n \ GL(m,Q̂)^n / GL(m,Q̂)_diag, with m = rank M. This space parametrizes the relative position of the n integral Betti structures inside the common adelic realization.

The page breaks off with 'the preceding considerations show that the transcendence degree of the points in question ...'. Presumably he means that the field generated over Q by the coordinates of this Q̂-point has transcendence degree bounded by the dimension of the Q-variety (∏ P_i)/G, roughly (n-1)·dim G. Possibly he also wanted equality in the generic case, as an ℓ-adic/adelic analogue of his period conjecture. The thread is unfinished.
errors: Q̂ is written as the full product ∏ Q_ℓ rather than the finite adeles A_f. This is harmless: the comparison isomorphisms are integral for almost all ℓ, so the point actually lies in the restricted product.
'Place v' must mean a complex embedding k -> C, not a valuation; k is algebraically closed, so it has no interesting archimedean places in the usual sense.

The final double coset space forgets the G-structure. The finer invariant lives in the G-torsor quotient (∏ P_i)/G, or in G-type double cosets G(Q)\G(A_f)/K. For GL_m alone the relevant class sets over Q are trivial, so the GL(m) version loses most of the information.
The existence of a Q-valued fibre functor is unproblematic here, since any Betti realization provides one. The notation 'ξ_0 ∈ T(Q)' is unclear on the page.

ideas.what: Integral Betti lattices for different complex embeddings of the base field, all sitting in the common adelic (étale) realization
ideas.modern_name: Betti structures of conjugate varieties / adelic comparison; Serre's conjugate varieties phenomenon

ideas.what: Torsor Isom^⊗(ω_σ, ω_τ) between Betti fibre functors for two embeddings, under the motivic Galois group, with a canonical adelic point coming from étale comparison
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of comparison between conjugate Betti realizations; key ingredient of the Taniyama group and of the conjugation of Shimura varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, LNM 900, 1982); Langlands (1979); Milne–Shih

ideas.what: Invariant point in (∏P_i)/G(Q̂) and in GL(m,Ẑ)^n\GL(m,Q̂)^n/GL(m,Q̂), measuring the relative position of the lattices
ideas.modern_name: Adelic double coset / genus-class invariant of lattices

ideas.what: Transcendence degree of the adelic comparison points, bounded via the dimension of the torsor quotient
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic/adelic analogue of the Grothendieck period conjecture for comparisons between conjugate embeddings
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (complex period version: Grothendieck, via Lang 1966; André)

missed.claim: Around 1969–72 Grothendieck already formulates the comparison between Betti realizations of a motive under different complex embeddings as a torsor under the motivic Galois group, carrying a canonical adelic point coming from étale comparison. This is the structure later central to Deligne's and Langlands' work on conjugation of Shimura varieties and the Taniyama group (1979–82).
missed.quote: P_i = Isom(ξ, ξ_{v_i}) sous G^f_{M ξ_0} (sur Q) et on a un point dans (∏P_i)(Q̂)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: the torsor viewpoint on conjugate Betti realizations predates its published appearance by about a decade.

missed.claim: A transcendence statement about the adelic comparison points relating Betti lattices of different embeddings. It reads as an ℓ-adic analogue of the period conjecture, with the dimension of the torsor quotient (∏P_i)/G bounding the transcendence degree.
missed.quote: Les considérations qui précèdent montrent que le degré de transcendance des pts en question
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Adelic or ℓ-adic 'periods' comparing conjugate embeddings, and their transcendence, are little studied compared with complex and p-adic periods. A precise conjecture here could connect the dimension of the motivic Galois group to arithmetic of conjugate varieties.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an early, explicit Tannakian torsor formulation of comparison between conjugate Betti realizations with its adelic point, anticipating Deligne/Langlands. It also starts an unusual transcendence-degree thread for adelic comparison points that is not completed. The core construction is now standard, so the surprise is moderate.

Marginal note reads 'G agissant diagonalement', attached to the point of [(∏P_i)/G](Q̂).
Right margin of the double coset line: 'm = rang M'.
'foncteur fibre de référence (qui est défini sur Q)' is uncertain; it is likely 'un foncteur fibre de référence (qui existe défini sur Q)'.
